name: bodesign
description: AI PCB design copilot — ingest a KiCad/EDA project folder, plan requirements, source reference evidence, generate KiCad symbols/schematics, lay out + export fab files, and track readiness, validated against KiCad and a known-good reference (control group). Runs as a Docker container; MCP Streamable HTTP over a Unix socket with a token file API.
instructions:
bodesign exposes AI PCB-design tools (prefix `bodesign_`): stage_dir, ingest_project, plan_design_intent, evidence_manifest, emit_symbol, compose_schematic, pin_allocation, emit_layout, emit_fab, render_companion, emit_doc, package_readiness, reference_crosscheck.

FILE MODEL (docxmcp-style). Upload your whole project tree as a tarball:
  tar -C dir -cf - . | curl --unix-socket .../.run/bodesign.sock -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' --data-binary @- http://bodesign.local/files
-> returns {token, doc_dir, files}. Or call `bodesign_stage_dir` with an inline {relpath:{content,encoding}} map. Then pass `token` to any tool: its path args (folder/out_dir/path/...) resolve inside the token's doc_dir, and the result lists produced files as {rel, url}. Download them:
  curl --unix-socket .../.run/bodesign.sock http://bodesign.local/files/{token}/blob/{rel}
Tools also accept plain host paths for the local same-host UDS case.

The server is also reachable over TCP HTTP at http://<host>:8077/mcp/ (same API; the container publishes both the UDS and :8077).

No send-to-fab output without deterministic validation + explicit user approval. Reliability is shown by cross-check vs a known-good reference (control group), not asserted.
